ko.title: [마케팅 101 #5] 왜 "모두"가 추격할 수 있는 최악의 고객인가

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > 시장 세분화는 광범위한 시장을 다르게 행동하는 사람 그룹으로 나누는 행위입니다 — 따라서 모두에게 외치는 것을 멈추고 특정 누군가에게 말하기를 시작할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: 첫 번째 창업자에게 고객이 누구인지 물어보면, 종종 이렇게 들을 수 있습니다: "솔직히?

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: 이것이 필요한 누구든지."

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: 그 답변은 야심차 보입니다.

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: 실제로는 비즈니스에서 가장 비용이 많이 드는 문장입니다.

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: 당신의 고객이 모두라면, 당신의 광고는 모두에게 호소해야 하고, 당신의 가격은 모두를 위해 작동해야 하며, 당신의 제품은 모두를 위해 조금 맞아야 합니다 — 이는 보통 아무에게도 정확히 맞지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **시장 세분화**가 해결책입니다.

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: 시장을 부분군으로 나누는 과정으로, 각 부분군의 구성원들은 서로 유사하면서 다른 그룹들과는 *구매 행동에 중요한* 방식으로 다릅니다.

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: 이는 고전적인 STP 수열에서 "S"입니다: **세분화 → 타겟팅 → 포지셔닝**.

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: 먼저 세분화하고 (이 시장은 자연스럽게 어떻게 나뉘는가?), 그 다음 어떤 조각을 제공할지 선택한 후, 그들에게 무엇을 의미할지 결정하십시오.

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: 사람들을 헷갈리게 하는 한 가지: 세그먼트를 *만드는* 것이 아니라는 것입니다.

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: 당신은 그들을 *발견*합니다.

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: 차이점은 이미 사람들의 지갑과 달력에 나타나 있습니다.

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: 당신의 일은 실제의 분할선을 찾는 것입니다.

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### 세분화 변수의 네 가지 유형

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: 마케터들은 네 가지 광범위한 **기준** (시장을 분할하는 변수들)을 사용하여 시장을 나눕니다:

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **지역적** — 지역, 기후, 도시 대 교외, 우편번호. 제설기는 미니애폴리스에서 피닉스보다 다르게 판매됩니다.

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **인구통계적** — 나이, 수입, 성별, 가구 규모, 교육 수준, 인생 단계. 측정하기 쉽고, 미디어 구매 타겟팅도 쉽습니다.

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **심리특성적** — 가치관, 생활방식, 성격, 자기 이미지, 정체성. 누군가가 *왜* 구매하는지.

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **행동 기반** — 사용 빈도, 구매 시기, 추구하는 이점, 충성도 상태, 가격 민감도. *그들이 실제로 하는 것.*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: 대부분의 경험 많은 마케터들이 도달하는 실용적인 계층구조는 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: 인구통계는 당신에게 **누구**인지 알려줍니다.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: 심리특성은 당신에게 **왜**인지 알려줍니다.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: 행동은 당신에게 **그들이 실제로 돈으로 무엇을 했는지** 알려줍니다 — 그리고 행동은 보통 그들이 다음에 무엇을 할지의 가장 강한 예측 변수입니다.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: 오스틴에 사는 동일한 수입의 34세 두 명은 고객으로서 공통점이 없을 수 있습니다; 한 명은 10년 동안 같은 브랜드를 구매하고, 다른 한 명은 쿠폰이 있을 때마다 바꿉니다.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: 문제는: 행동은 누군가가 고객이 되기 *전에* 관찰하기 어렵다는 것입니다.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: 그래서 일반적인 워크플로우는 **행동과 필요로 세분화한 후 인구통계로 프로필 작성**하는 것입니다 — 인구통계야말로 광고 플랫폼, 메일링 리스트, 또는 매장 위치 결정에서 실제로 이들을 찾을 수 있게 해주기 때문입니다.

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### 세그먼트가 보유할 가치가 있을 때는?

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: 이름 붙일 수 있는 모든 그룹이 추격할 가치가 있는 세그먼트는 아닙니다.

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: 표준 체크리스트:

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **측정 가능** — 크기를 결정하고 설명할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **충분한 규모** — 노력할 가치가 있을 정도로 충분히 큽니다.

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **접근 가능** — 미디어와 배포를 통해 실제로 도달할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **차별화 가능** — 다른 세그먼트와 달리 당신의 제안에 다르게 반응합니다. (이것은 사람들이 건너뛰는 부분이자, 세분화를 *세분화*가 아닌 잡담으로 만드는 부분입니다.)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **실행 가능** — 그것을 잘 제공할 리소스가 있습니다.

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: 일반 산술로 그 규모를 추정하는 대략적인 방법:

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: 그 다음 그들에게 도달하고 제공하는 데 드는 비용을 뺍니다.

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: 저렴하게 도달할 수 없는 거대한 세그먼트는 찾기 쉬운 작은 세그먼트보다 가치가 적습니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## 일상에서: 1월 헬스장 러시

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: 매년 1월, 대략 같은 결심 — "몸매를 다시 만들겠다" — 수백만 명의 미국인들을 헬스장을 찾도록 보냅니다.

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: 외부에서 보면 한 시장처럼 보입니다.

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: 실제로는 최소한 네 개입니다.

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness**는 한 달에 약 $15에 Classic 회원권을 판매하고, 그 장소를 보라색과 노란색으로 장식하며, 그것을 "판단 없는 구역"이라고 부릅니다.

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: 그 슬로건은 장식이 아닙니다 — 그것은 *운동하고 싶지만* 숨을 헐떡이는 파워리프터들의 행렬을 지나갈 때 자의식을 느끼는 사람들을 겨냥한 심리특성적 명중입니다.

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: 행동 기반의 측면도 주목하세요: 매우 큰 회원 기반 전체에 걸친 매우 낮은 가격이 정확히 작동하는 이유는 평균 회원이 그렇게 자주 나타나지 않기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: 가벼운 사용자들이, 이례적으로, 수익성이 있는 사용자들입니다.

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox**는 주요 시장에서 월 $200 이상을 청구하며, 유명하게도, 한 번 "We don't speak gym"이라고 말하는 캠페인을 실행했습니다.

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: 같은 광범위한 카테고리, 정반대 세그먼트: 클럽이 지위 재화이자 생활방식 신호인 사람들, 최소화할 항목이 아닌.

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **CrossFit 박스**는 일반적으로 Planet Fitness가 의도적으로 판매하지 않는 것 — 당신의 이름을 알고 있는 코치와 오전 6시

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: 당신이 빠졌을 때 알아채는 클래스 — 을 위해 월 $150–$250을 청구합니다.

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: 추구하는 이점은 책임감과 공동체입니다.

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **집에서 구매하는 사람** — Peloton, 조절 가능한 덤벨 세트, YouTube 구독 — 는 수입보다 인생 단계로 더 자주 세분화됩니다: 오전 6시에 집을 떠날 수 없는 어린 자녀를 둔 부모.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: 이제 중요한 부분입니다.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox는 Planet Fitness에 지고 있지 않습니다.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: 그들은 거의 같은 경쟁에 있지 않습니다.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: 각각은 다르게 행동하는 그룹을 중심으로 제품, 가격, 위치 전략, 그리고 목소리 톤을 구축했습니다 — 그리고 각각은 다른 것들을 이기려고 노력하면서 자신을 손상시킬 것입니다.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: $15 Equinox는 자신의 신호를 파괴할 것입니다.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: 모든 코너에 개인 코치가 있는 Planet Fitness는 자신의 비용 구조를 폭발시키고 그것이 위해 지어진 정확한 사람들을 겁주었을 것입니다.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: 그것이 세분화가 자신의 일을 하는 것입니다: 고객을 설명하는 것이 아니라, *당신이 나쁜 것을 할 의향이 있는 것을 결정*하는 것.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. 세분화는 광범위한 시장을 다르게 반응하는 그룹으로 나눕니다 — 이는 STP의 첫 번째 단계이며, "모두"는 세그먼트가 아닙니다.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. 네 가지 기준은 지역적, 인구통계적, 심리특성적, 행동 기반입니다; 행동이 가장 잘 예측하고, 인구통계가 가장 잘 도달하므로, 대부분의 마케터들은 행동으로 세분화하고 인구통계로 프로필을 작성합니다.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. 세그먼트는 측정 가능하고, 충분한 규모이고, 접근 가능하고, 차별화 가능하고, 실행 가능할 때만 제공할 가치가 있습니다 — 차별화 가능 테스트는 실제 세그먼트를 잡담과 분리하는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가진단

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a **behavioral** segmentation variable?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 다음 중 어느 것이 **행동 기반** 세분화 변수입니까?

segments.src: a) Household income
segments.tr: a) 가구 수입

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) 구매 시기 (예: 어머니날에 꽃 사기)

segments.src: c) ZIP code
segments.tr: c) 우편번호

segments.src: d) Age
segments.tr: d) 나이

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A segment of 40 million Americans who all say they want a product is automatically an attractive segment to target.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 모두 제품을 원한다고 말하는 4천만 명의 미국인 세그먼트는 자동으로 타겟팅할 매력적인 세그먼트입니다.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gym brands itself a "Judgement Free Zone" to appeal to people who feel intimidated by traditional gyms.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 헬스장은 전통적인 헬스장에 위협을 느끼는 사람들에게 호소하기 위해 자신을 "판단 없는 구역"으로 브랜드합니다.

segments.src: This is primarily which kind of segmentation?
segments.tr: 이것은 주로 어떤 종류의 세분화입니까?

segments.src: a) Geographic
segments.tr: a) 지역적

segments.src: b) Demographic
segments.tr: b) 인구통계적

segments.src: c) Psychographic
segments.tr: c) 심리특성적

segments.src: d) Loyalty-based
segments.tr: d) 충성도 기반

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Market segmentation** — Dividing a broad market into subgroups that are internally similar and behave differently from one another in ways that affect buying.
segments.tr: - **시장 세분화** — 광범위한 시장을 내부적으로 유사하고 구매에 영향을 미치는 방식으로 서로 다르게 행동하는 부분군으로 나누기.

segments.src: - **Segmentation base** — The variable you cut the market on (age, region, usage rate, values, and so on).
segments.tr: - **세분화 기준** — 시장을 분할하는 변수 (나이, 지역, 사용 빈도, 가치관 등).

segments.src: - **Demographic segmentation** — Grouping by observable population traits: age, income, gender, household size, life stage.
segments.tr: - **인구통계적 세분화** — 관찰 가능한 인구 특성으로 그룹화: 나이, 수입, 성별, 가구 규모, 인생 단계.

segments.src: - **Psychographic segmentation** — Grouping by values, lifestyle, personality, and self-image — the *why* behind a purchase.
segments.tr: - **심리특성적 세분화** — 가치관, 생활방식, 성격, 자기 이미지로 그룹화 — 구매 뒤의 *왜*.

segments.src: - **Behavioral segmentation** — Grouping by what people actually do: how often they buy, on what occasion, which benefit they're after, how loyal or price-sensitive they are.
segments.tr: - **행동 기반 세분화** — 사람들이 실제로 하는 것으로 그룹화: 얼마나 자주 구매하는지, 어떤 시기에, 어떤 이점을 추구하는지, 얼마나 충성도가 높거나 가격에 민감한지.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — b.** Occasion is about buying behavior; income, ZIP code, and age are demographic or geographic descriptors.
segments.tr: *답변: **Q1 — b.** 시기는 구매 행동에 관한 것입니다; 수입, 우편번호, 나이는 인구통계적 또는 지역적 설명자입니다.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** Size is only one of five tests.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (거짓).** 규모는 다섯 가지 테스트 중 하나일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: A giant segment that you can't reach affordably, that doesn't respond differently to your offer, or that you lack the resources to serve is not attractive — "substantial" without "accessible," "differentiable," and "actionable" is a trap.
segments.tr: 저렴하게 도달할 수 없는 거대한 세그먼트, 당신의 제안에 다르게 반응하지 않는 세그먼트, 또는 제공할 리소스가 없는 세그먼트는 매력적이지 않습니다 — "접근 가능", "차별화 가능", "실행 가능" 없이 "충분한 규모"는 함정입니다.

segments.src: **Q3 — c.** It targets a feeling and self-image (exercise anxiety, not wanting to be watched), which is psychographic — even though the brand will then use demographics like age and income to find those people in ad platforms.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — c.** 그것은 감정과 자기 이미지 (운동 불안, 관찰당하기를 원하지 않음)를 겨냥하며, 이는 심리특성적입니다 — 비록 브랜드가 광고 플랫폼에서 이런 사람들을 찾기 위해 나이와 수입 같은 인구통계를 사용할 것이지만.*

hi.title: [Marketing 101 #5] "सभी" आपके द्वारा पीछा किए जा सकने वाले सबसे बुरे ग्राहक क्यों हैं

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > बाजार विभाजन एक व्यापक बाजार को उन लोगों के समूहों में विभाजित करने का कार्य है जो अलग तरीके से व्यवहार करते हैं — ताकि आप सभी को चिल्लाना बंद कर सकें और किसी विशिष्ट व्यक्ति से बात कर सकें।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: एक पहली बार संस्थापक से पूछें कि उनका ग्राहक कौन है, और आप अक्सर सुनेंगे: "ईमानदारी से?

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: कोई भी जिसे इसकी आवश्यकता है।"

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: वह उत्तर महत्वाकांक्षी लगता है।

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: यह वास्तव में व्यवसाय में सबसे महंगा वाक्य है।

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: यदि आपका ग्राहक सभी हैं, तो आपका विज्ञापन सभी को आकर्षित करना होगा, आपकी कीमत सभी के लिए काम करनी होगी, और आपका उत्पाद सभी के लिए थोड़ा सही होना होगा — जिसका मतलब आमतौर पर यह है कि यह किसी के लिए भी बिल्कुल सही नहीं है।

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **बाजार विभाजन** समाधान है।

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: यह एक बाजार को उप-समूहों में विभाजित करने की प्रक्रिया है जिसके सदस्य एक-दूसरे के समान हैं और अन्य समूहों से ऐसे तरीकों से भिन्न हैं जो *क्रय व्यवहार के लिए महत्वपूर्ण* हैं।

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: यह क्लासिक STP अनुक्रम में "S" है: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**।

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: पहले Segment करें (यह बाजार स्वाभाविक रूप से कैसे विभाजित होता है?), फिर चुनें कि किन स्लाइसों को सेवा देनी है, फिर तय करें कि आप उनके लिए क्या मायने रखते हैं।

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: एक बात जो लोगों को भ्रमित करती है: आप segments को *बनाते* नहीं हैं।

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: आप उन्हें *खोजते* हैं।

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: अंतर पहले से ही लोगों की जेब और कैलेंडर में हैं।

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: आपका काम असली कट लाइनें खोजना है।

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### विभाजन चर के चार परिवार

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: मार्केटर्स **bases** के चार व्यापक प्रकारों का उपयोग करके बाजारों को विभाजित करते हैं (वे चर जिन पर आप कट करते हैं):

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **भौगोलिक** — क्षेत्र, जलवायु, शहर बनाम उपनगर, ZIP कोड। स्नो ब्लोअर मिनिएपोलिस में फिनिक्स की तुलना में अलग तरीके से बिकते हैं।

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **जनसांख्यिकीय** — आयु, आय, लिंग, घरेलू आकार, शिक्षा, जीवन चरण। मापने में आसान, मीडिया खरीदने में आसान।

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **साइकोग्राफिक** — मूल्य, जीवनशैली, व्यक्तित्व, आत्म-छवि, पहचान। *क्यों* कोई खरीदता है।

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **व्यवहारात्मक** — उपयोग दर, खरीद अवसर, मांगे गए लाभ, वफादारी स्थिति, मूल्य संवेदनशीलता। *वे वास्तव में क्या करते हैं।*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: यहाँ सबसे अनुभवी मार्केटर्स द्वारा अपनाया जाने वाला व्यावहारिक पदानुक्रम है।

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: जनसांख्यिकी आपको बताती है **कौन**।

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: साइकोग्राफिक्स आपको बताते हैं **क्यों**।

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: व्यवहार आपको बताता है **उन्होंने वास्तव में अपने पैसे के साथ क्या किया** — और व्यवहार आमतौर पर यह सबसे मजबूत भविष्यद्वाणी है कि वे आगे क्या करेंगे।

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: ऑस्टिन में समान आय वाले दो 34 वर्षीय ग्राहकों के रूप में कुछ भी समान नहीं हो सकते हैं; एक दशक के लिए एक ही ब्रांड खरीदता है, दूसरा हर बार जब कूपन होता है स्विच करता है।

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: समस्या: किसी के ग्राहक बनने से *पहले* व्यवहार का अवलोकन करना मुश्किल है।

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: तो सामान्य वर्कफ़्लो **व्यवहार और आवश्यकताओं पर सेगमेंट करना है, फिर जनसांख्यिकी के साथ प्रोफाइल करना** — क्योंकि जनसांख्यिकी वह है जो आपको विज्ञापन प्लेटफॉर्म, मेलिंग सूची, या स्टोर स्थान निर्णय में वास्तव में इन लोगों को खोजने देती है।

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### एक सेगमेंट कब रखने लायक है?

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: हर समूह जिसका नाम आप दे सकते हैं, वह एक सेगमेंट नहीं है जो पीछा करने लायक है।

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: मानक चेकलिस्ट:

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **मापने योग्य** — आप इसका आकार और वर्णन कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **पर्याप्त** — प्रयास के लायक बड़ा।

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **सुलभ** — आप वास्तव में इसे मीडिया और वितरण के साथ पहुंच सकते हैं।

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **विभेदक** — यह अन्य सेगमेंट की तुलना में आपके ऑफर के लिए अलग तरीके से प्रतिक्रिया देता है। (यह वह है जिसे लोग छोड़ते हैं, और यह वह है जो सेगमेंटेशन को *सेगमेंटेशन* बनाता है बजाय तुच्छता के।)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **कार्यवाहीयोग्य** — आपके पास इसे अच्छी तरह सेवा देने के संसाधन हैं।

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: एक को आकार देने का एक मोटा तरीका, सादे अंकगणित में:

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: फिर उन्हें पहुंचने और सेवा देने की लागत घटाएं।

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: एक विशाल सेगमेंट जिसे आप सस्ते में नहीं पहुंच सकते, एक छोटे सेगमेंट से कम मूल्यवान है जिसे खोजना आसान है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में: जनवरी जिम भीड़

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: हर जनवरी, लगभग वही संकल्प — "फिट रहो" — लाखों अमेरिकियों को जिम खोजने के लिए भेजता है।

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: बाहर से यह एक बाजार की तरह लगता है।

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: यह कम से कम चार हैं।

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness** एक क्लासिक सदस्यता लगभग $15 प्रति माह के लिए बेचता है, जगह को बैंगनी और पीले रंग में लपेटता है, और इसे "Judgement Free Zone" कहता है।

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: वह टैगलाइन सजावट नहीं है — यह एक साइकोग्राफिक बुलसआई है जो उन लोगों को लक्षित करता है जो *व्यायाम करना चाहते हैं* लेकिन गड़गड़ाते हुए पावरलिफ्टर्स की पंक्ति के पास चलने से शर्मिंदा महसूस करते हैं।

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: व्यवहारात्मक कोण को भी देखें: एक बहुत कम कीमत एक बहुत बड़े सदस्य आधार के आर-पार काम करती है क्योंकि औसत सदस्य अक्सर दिखाई नहीं देता।

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: हल्के उपयोगकर्ता असामान्य रूप से, लाभजनक वाले हैं।

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox** प्रमुख बाजारों में $200 से अधिक प्रति माह चार्ज करता है और, प्रसिद्ध रूप से, एक बार एक अभियान चलाया जो कहता था "हम जिम नहीं बोलते हैं।"

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: एक ही व्यापक श्रेणी, विपरीत सेगमेंट: वे लोग जिनके लिए क्लब एक स्थिति वस्तु और जीवनशैली संकेत है, कम करने के लिए एक पंक्ति आइटम नहीं।

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **एक CrossFit box** आमतौर पर $150–$250 प्रति माह चलाता है कुछ के लिए जो Planet Fitness जानबूझकर नहीं बेचता — एक कोच जो आपका नाम जानता है और सुबह 6 बजे।

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: कक्षा जो देखती है जब आप गायब हैं।

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: मांगा जाने वाला लाभ जवाबदेही और समुदाय है।

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **घर पर खरीदार** — Peloton, समायोज्य डम्बल का एक सेट, एक YouTube सदस्यता — अक्सर आय से अधिक जीवन चरण द्वारा विभाजित होते हैं: छोटे बच्चों वाला माता-पिता जो सचमुच सुबह 6 बजे घर नहीं छोड़ सकता।

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: अब महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा।

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox Planet Fitness को हार नहीं रहा है।

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: वे मुश्किल से एक ही लड़ाई में हैं।

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: प्रत्येक ने एक उत्पाद, एक कीमत, एक स्थान रणनीति, और एक समूह के चारों ओर आवाज का एक स्वर बनाया जो अलग तरीके से व्यवहार करता है — और प्रत्येक दूसरों को जीतने की कोशिश करके अपने आप को नुकसान पहुंचाएगा।

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: एक $15 Equinox अपने स्वयं के संकेत को नष्ट कर देगा।

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: हर कोने में व्यक्तिगत कोच के साथ एक Planet Fitness अपनी लागत संरचना को उड़ा देगा और उन सटीक लोगों को डराएगा जिनके लिए यह बनाया गया था।

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: यह सेगमेंटेशन अपना काम कर रहा है: ग्राहकों का वर्णन नहीं, बल्कि *यह तय करना कि आप किस चीज में खराब होने के लिए तैयार हैं*।

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3-लाइन सारांश

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. सेगमेंटेशन एक व्यापक बाजार को उन समूहों में विभाजित करता है जो अलग तरीके से प्रतिक्रिया देते हैं — यह STP का पहला चरण है, और "सभी" एक सेगमेंट नहीं है।

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. चार आधार भौगोलिक, जनसांख्यिकीय, साइकोग्राफिक, और व्यवहारात्मक हैं; व्यवहार सर्वश्रेष्ठ भविष्यद्वाणी करता है, जनसांख्यिकी सर्वश्रेष्ठ पहुंचते हैं, इसलिए अधिकांश मार्केटर्स व्यवहार पर सेगमेंट करते हैं और जनसांख्यिकी के साथ प्रोफाइल करते हैं।

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. एक सेगमेंट केवल सेवा देने के लायक है यदि यह मापने योग्य, पर्याप्त, सुलभ, विभेदक, और कार्यवाहीयोग्य है — विभेदक परीक्षा वह है जो वास्तविक सेगमेंट को तुच्छता से अलग करता है।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-प्रश्नोत्तरी

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a **behavioral** segmentation variable?
segments.tr: **Q1.** इनमें से कौन सा **व्यवहारात्मक** सेगमेंटेशन चर है?

segments.src: a) Household income
segments.tr: a) घरेलू आय

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) खरीद अवसर (जैसे, माता दिवस के लिए फूल खरीदना)

segments.src: c) ZIP code
segments.tr: c) ZIP कोड

segments.src: d) Age
segments.tr: d) आयु

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A segment of 40 million Americans who all say they want a product is automatically an attractive segment to target.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 40 मिलियन अमेरिकियों का एक सेगमेंट जो सभी कहते हैं कि वे एक उत्पाद चाहते हैं, स्वचालित रूप से लक्षित करने के लिए एक आकर्षक सेगमेंट है।

segments.src: **Q3.** A gym brands itself a "Judgement Free Zone" to appeal to people who feel intimidated by traditional gyms.
segments.tr: **Q3.** एक जिम अपने आप को "Judgement Free Zone" के रूप में ब्रांड करता है उन लोगों को अपील करने के लिए जो पारंपरिक जिमों से डराए हुए महसूस करते हैं।

segments.src: This is primarily which kind of segmentation?
segments.tr: यह मुख्य रूप से किस प्रकार का सेगमेंटेशन है?

segments.src: a) Geographic
segments.tr: a) भौगोलिक

segments.src: b) Demographic
segments.tr: b) जनसांख्यिकीय

segments.src: c) Psychographic
segments.tr: c) साइकोग्राफिक

segments.src: d) Loyalty-based
segments.tr: d) वफादारी-आधारित

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **Market segmentation** — Dividing a broad market into subgroups that are internally similar and behave differently from one another in ways that affect buying.
segments.tr: - **बाजार विभाजन** — एक व्यापक बाजार को उप-समूहों में विभाजित करना जो आंतरिक रूप से समान हैं और एक-दूसरे से अलग तरीकों से व्यवहार करते हैं जो खरीद को प्रभावित करते हैं।

segments.src: - **Segmentation base** — The variable you cut the market on (age, region, usage rate, values, and so on).
segments.tr: - **विभाजन आधार** — वह चर जिस पर आप बाजार को काटते हैं (आयु, क्षेत्र, उपयोग दर, मूल्य, आदि)।

segments.src: - **Demographic segmentation** — Grouping by observable population traits: age, income, gender, household size, life stage.
segments.tr: - **जनसांख्यिकीय सेगमेंटेशन** — अवलोकनीय जनसंख्या विशेषताओं द्वारा समूहन: आयु, आय, लिंग, घरेलू आकार, जीवन चरण।

segments.src: - **Psychographic segmentation** — Grouping by values, lifestyle, personality, and self-image — the *why* behind a purchase.
segments.tr: - **साइकोग्राफिक सेगमेंटेशन** — मूल्यों, जीवनशैली, व्यक्तित्व, और आत्म-छवि द्वारा समूहन — खरीद के पीछे का *क्यों*।

segments.src: - **Behavioral segmentation** — Grouping by what people actually do: how often they buy, on what occasion, which benefit they're after, how loyal or price-sensitive they are.
segments.tr: - **व्यवहारात्मक सेगमेंटेशन** — लोग वास्तव में क्या करते हैं इसके आधार पर समूहन: वे कितनी बार खरीदते हैं, किस अवसर पर, वे किस लाभ के बाद हैं, वे कितने वफादार या मूल्य संवेदनशील हैं।

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — b.** Occasion is about buying behavior; income, ZIP code, and age are demographic or geographic descriptors.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **Q1 — b.** अवसर खरीद व्यवहार के बारे में है; आय, ZIP कोड, और आयु जनसांख्यिकीय या भौगोलिक विवरणकर्ता हैं।

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** Size is only one of five tests.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (गलत)।** आकार पाँच परीक्षणों में से केवल एक है।

segments.src: A giant segment that you can't reach affordably, that doesn't respond differently to your offer, or that you lack the resources to serve is not attractive — "substantial" without "accessible," "differentiable," and "actionable" is a trap.
segments.tr: एक विशाल सेगमेंट जिसे आप सस्ते में नहीं पहुंच सकते, जो आपके ऑफर के लिए अलग तरीके से प्रतिक्रिया नहीं देता, या जिसके लिए आपके पास संसाधनों की कमी है, आकर्षक नहीं है — "सुलभ," "विभेदक," और "कार्यवाहीयोग्य" के बिना "पर्याप्त" एक जाल है।

segments.src: **Q3 — c.** It targets a feeling and self-image (exercise anxiety, not wanting to be watched), which is psychographic — even though the brand will then use demographics like age and income to find those people in ad platforms.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — c.** यह एक भावना और आत्म-छवि (व्यायाम चिंता, देखे जाने की इच्छा न करना) को लक्षित करता है, जो साइकोग्राफिक है — भले ही ब्रांड तब विज्ञापन प्लेटफॉर्म में उन लोगों को खोजने के लिए आयु और आय जैसी जनसांख्यिकी का उपयोग करेगा।*

es.title: [Marketing 101 #5] Por Qué "Todos" Es el Peor Cliente Que Puedes Perseguir

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > La segmentación de mercado es el acto de dividir un mercado amplio en grupos de personas que se comportan de manera diferente, para que puedas dejar de hablar a todos y empieces a dirigirte a alguien.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: Pregúntale a un emprendedor por primera vez quién es su cliente, y a menudo escucharás: "Honestamente?

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: Cualquiera que lo necesite."

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: Esa respuesta suena ambiciosa.

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: Es en realidad la frase más cara en los negocios.

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: Si tu cliente es todos, entonces tu anuncio tiene que atraer a todos, tu precio tiene que funcionar para todos, y tu producto tiene que ser un poco correcto para todos — lo que generalmente significa que no es exactamente correcto para nadie.

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **La segmentación de mercado** es la solución.

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: Es el proceso de dividir un mercado en subgrupos cuyos miembros se parecen entre sí y difieren de otros grupos de maneras que *importan para el comportamiento de compra*.

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: Es la "S" en la secuencia clásica STP: **Segmentación → Orientación → Posicionamiento**.

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: Segmenta primero (¿cómo se divide naturalmente este mercado?), luego elige qué segmentos servir, luego decide qué significarás para ellos.

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: Una cosa que confunde a la gente: no *creas* segmentos.

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: Los *descubres*.

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: Las diferencias ya están ahí en los bolsillos y calendarios de las personas.

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: Tu trabajo es encontrar las líneas de corte que son reales.

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### Las cuatro familias de variables de segmentación

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: Los especialistas en marketing dividen los mercados usando cuatro tipos amplios de **bases** (las variables en las que cortas):

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **Geográfica** — región, clima, ciudad vs. suburbio, código postal. Las máquinas quitanieves se venden de manera diferente en Minneapolis que en Phoenix.

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **Demográfica** — edad, ingresos, género, tamaño del hogar, educación, etapa de vida. Fácil de medir, fácil de comprar medios de comunicación.

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **Psicográfica** — valores, estilo de vida, personalidad, autoimagen, identidad. *Por qué* alguien compra.

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **Conductual** — tasa de uso, ocasión de compra, beneficios buscados, estado de lealtad, sensibilidad al precio. *Lo que realmente hacen*.

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: Aquí está la jerarquía práctica en la que aterrizan la mayoría de los especialistas en marketing experimentados.

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: La demografía te dice **quién**.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: La psicografía te dice **por qué**.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: El comportamiento te dice **qué hicieron realmente con su dinero** — y el comportamiento es generalmente el predictor más fuerte de lo que harán a continuación.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: Dos personas de 34 años en Austin con ingresos idénticos pueden no tener nada en común como clientes; uno compra la misma marca durante una década, el otro cambia cada vez que hay un cupón.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: El inconveniente: el comportamiento es difícil de observar *antes de* que alguien se convierta en cliente.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: Entonces, el flujo de trabajo común es **segmentar por comportamiento y necesidades, luego perfilar con datos demográficos** — porque los datos demográficos son lo que te permite encontrar realmente a estas personas en una plataforma publicitaria, una lista de correo o una decisión de ubicación de tienda.

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### ¿Cuándo vale la pena tener un segmento?

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: No todo grupo que puedas nombrar es un segmento que valga la pena perseguir.

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: La lista de verificación estándar:

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **Medible** — puedes dimensionarlo y describirlo.

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **Sustancial** — lo suficientemente grande para justificar el esfuerzo.

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **Accesible** — realmente puedes alcanzarlo con medios y distribución.

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **Diferenciable** — responde a tu oferta de manera diferente a como lo hacen otros segmentos. (Este es el que la gente se salta, y es el que hace que la segmentación sea *segmentación* en lugar de trivialidades.)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **Accionable** — tienes los recursos para servirlo bien.

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: Una forma aproximada de dimensionar uno, en aritmética simple:

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: Luego resta lo que cuesta alcanzarlos y servirlos.

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: Un segmento enorme que no puedes alcanzar barato vale menos que uno pequeño que es fácil de encontrar.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana: El Ajetreo de Gimnasios de Enero

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: Cada enero, aproximadamente la misma resolución — "ponerse en forma" — envía a millones de estadounidenses a buscar un gimnasio.

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: Desde afuera parece un solo mercado.

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: Son al menos cuatro.

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness** vende una membresía Clásica por alrededor de $15 al mes, decora el lugar en púrpura y amarillo, y lo llama una "Zona Libre de Prejuicios".

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: Ese eslogan no es decoración — es un punto de mira psicográfico dirigido a personas que *quieren* hacer ejercicio pero se sienten cohibidas caminando pasado una fila de levantadores de pesas gruñendo.

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: Nota también el ángulo conductual: un precio muy bajo en una base de miembros muy grande funciona precisamente porque el miembro promedio no aparece tan a menudo.

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: Los usuarios ligeros son, inusualmente, los rentables.

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox** cobra bien por encima de $200 al mes en mercados importantes y, famosamente, una vez dirigió una campaña que decía "No hablamos gimnasio".

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: Misma categoría amplia, segmento opuesto: personas para quienes el club es un bien de estatus y una señal de estilo de vida, no una partida de línea a minimizar.

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **Un box de CrossFit** típicamente cuesta $150–$250 al mes por algo que Planet Fitness deliberadamente no vende — un entrenador que conoce tu nombre y una clase de las 6 a.m.

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: que nota cuando te falta.

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: El beneficio buscado es responsabilidad y comunidad.

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **El comprador en casa** — Peloton, un conjunto de mancernas ajustables, una suscripción de YouTube — a menudo se segmenta más por etapa de vida que por ingresos: un padre con hijos pequeños que literalmente no puede dejar la casa a las 6 a.m.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: Ahora la parte importante.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox no está perdiendo contra Planet Fitness.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: Apenas están en la misma pelea.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: Cada uno construyó un producto, un precio, una estrategia de ubicación y un tono de voz alrededor de un grupo que se comporta diferente — y cada uno se dañaría a sí mismo intentando ganar a los otros.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: Un Equinox de $15 destruiría su propia señal.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: Un Planet Fitness con entrenadores personales en cada rincón explotaría su estructura de costos y espantaría a las personas exactas para las que fue construido.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: Eso es la segmentación haciendo su trabajo: no describir clientes, sino *decidir en qué estás dispuesto a ser malo*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de 3 Líneas

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. La segmentación divide un mercado amplio en grupos que responden de manera diferente — es el primer paso del STP, y "todos" no es un segmento.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. Las cuatro bases son geográfica, demográfica, psicográfica y conductual; el comportamiento predice mejor, la demografía llega mejor, así que la mayoría de los especialistas en marketing segmentan por comportamiento y perfilan con datos demográficos.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. Un segmento solo vale la pena servir si es medible, sustancial, accesible, diferenciable y accionable — la prueba diferenciable es la que separa los segmentos reales de las trivialidades.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a **behavioral** segmentation variable?
segments.tr: **P1.** ¿Cuál de estos es una variable de segmentación **conductual**?

segments.src: a) Household income
segments.tr: a) Ingresos del hogar

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) Ocasión de compra (p. ej., comprar flores para el Día de la Madre)

segments.src: c) ZIP code
segments.tr: c) Código postal

segments.src: d) Age
segments.tr: d) Edad

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A segment of 40 million Americans who all say they want a product is automatically an attractive segment to target.
segments.tr: **P2.** (V/F) Un segmento de 40 millones de estadounidenses que todos dicen que quieren un producto es automáticamente un segmento atractivo para orientarse.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gym brands itself a "Judgement Free Zone" to appeal to people who feel intimidated by traditional gyms.
segments.tr: **P3.** Un gimnasio se marca a sí mismo como una "Zona Libre de Prejuicios" para atraer a personas que se sienten intimidadas por los gimnasios tradicionales.

segments.tr: ¿Esto es principalmente qué tipo de segmentación?

segments.tr: a) Geográfica

segments.tr: b) Demográfica

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **Market segmentation** — Dividing a broad market into subgroups that are internally similar and behave differently from one another in ways that affect buying.
segments.tr: - **Segmentación de mercado** — Dividir un mercado amplio en subgrupos que son internamente similares y se comportan de manera diferente entre sí de formas que afectan la compra.

segments.src: - **Segmentation base** — The variable you cut the market on (age, region, usage rate, values, and so on).
segments.tr: - **Base de segmentación** — La variable en la que cortas el mercado (edad, región, tasa de uso, valores, etc.).

segments.src: - **Demographic segmentation** — Grouping by observable population traits: age, income, gender, household size, life stage.
segments.tr: - **Segmentación demográfica** — Agrupación por características de población observables: edad, ingresos, género, tamaño del hogar, etapa de vida.

segments.src: - **Psychographic segmentation** — Grouping by values, lifestyle, personality, and self-image — the *why* behind a purchase.
segments.tr: - **Segmentación psicográfica** — Agrupación por valores, estilo de vida, personalidad e autoimagen — el *por qué* detrás de una compra.

segments.src: - **Behavioral segmentation** — Grouping by what people actually do: how often they buy, on what occasion, which benefit they're after, how loyal or price-sensitive they are.
segments.tr: - **Segmentación conductual** — Agrupación por lo que las personas realmente hacen: con qué frecuencia compran, en qué ocasión, qué beneficio persiguen, qué tan leales o sensibles al precio son.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — b.** Occasion is about buying behavior; income, ZIP code, and age are demographic or geographic descriptors.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **P1 — b.** La ocasión se trata de comportamiento de compra; el ingreso, código postal y edad son descriptores demográficos o geográficos.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** Size is only one of five tests.
segments.tr: **P2 — F (falso).** El tamaño es solo uno de cinco pruebas.

segments.src: A giant segment that you can't reach affordably, that doesn't respond differently to your offer, or that you lack the resources to serve is not attractive — "substantial" without "accessible," "differentiable," and "actionable" is a trap.
segments.tr: Un segmento gigante que no puedes alcanzar de manera asequible, que no responde de manera diferente a tu oferta, o que careces de los recursos para servir no es atractivo — "sustancial" sin "accesible", "diferenciable" y "accionable" es una trampa.

segments.src: **Q3 — c.** It targets a feeling and self-image (exercise anxiety, not wanting to be watched), which is psychographic — even though the brand will then use demographics like age and income to find those people in ad platforms.*
segments.tr: **P3 — c.** Se dirige a un sentimiento e imagen de sí mismo (ansiedad por el ejercicio, no querer ser visto), que es psicográfico — aunque la marca luego usará datos demográficos como edad e ingresos para encontrar a esas personas en plataformas publicitarias.*

ar.title: [Marketing 101 #5] لماذا "الجميع" هو أسوأ عميل يمكنك مطاردته

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > تقسيم السوق هو فعل تقسيم السوق الواسع إلى مجموعات من الأشخاص الذين يتصرفون بشكل مختلف — حتى تتمكن من التوقف عن الصراخ للجميع وبدء التحدث إلى شخص ما.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## المفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: اسأل مؤسس شركة للمرة الأولى من هو عميله، وغالباً ما تسمع: "بصراحة؟

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: أي شخص يحتاج إلى هذا."

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: هذه الإجابة تبدو طموحة.

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: إنها في الواقع أغلى جملة في الأعمال التجارية.

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: إذا كان عميلك الجميع، فيجب أن يستهدف إعلانك الجميع، وأن يعمل سعرك للجميع، وأن يكون منتجك صحيحاً قليلاً للجميع — مما يعني عادة أنه ليس صحيحاً لأحد.

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **تقسيم السوق** هو الحل.

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: إنه عملية تقسيم السوق إلى مجموعات فرعية تكون أعضاؤها متشابهين لبعضهم البعض ومختلفين عن المجموعات الأخرى بطرق *مهمة للسلوك الشرائي*.

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: إنها "S" في تسلسل STP الكلاسيكي: **التقسيم → الاستهداف → التموضع**.

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: قسّم أولاً (كيف ينقسم هذا السوق بشكل طبيعي؟)، ثم اختر الأجزاء التي ستخدمها، ثم قرر ما ستعنيه لهم.

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: شيء واحد يربك الناس: أنت لا *تنشئ* القطاعات.

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: أنت *تكتشفها*.

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: الاختلافات موجودة بالفعل في محافظ الناس وتقاويمهم.

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: وظيفتك هي إيجاد خطوط القطع التي حقيقية.

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### عائلات المتغيرات الأربع للتقسيم

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: يقسم المسوقون الأسواق باستخدام أربعة أنواع واسعة من **القواعس** (المتغيرات التي تقطع عليها):

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **الجغرافي** — المنطقة، المناخ، المدينة مقابل الضواحي، الرمز البريدي. تبيع أدوات تنظيف الثلج بشكل مختلف في Minneapolis عن Phoenix.

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **الديموغرافي** — العمر، الدخل، الجنس، حجم الأسرة، التعليم، مرحلة الحياة. سهل القياس، سهل شراء الوسائط ضده.

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **النفسي** — القيم، نمط الحياة، الشخصية، صورة الذات، الهوية. *لماذا* يشتري شخص ما.

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **السلوكي** — معدل الاستخدام، مناسبة الشراء، الفوائد المطلوبة، حالة الولاء، حساسية السعر. *ما الذي يفعلونه بالفعل.*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: إليك التسلسل الهرمي العملي الذي يصل إليه معظم المسوقين ذوي الخبرة.

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: البيانات الديموغرافية تخبرك **من**.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: النفسيات تخبرك **لماذا**.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: السلوك يخبرك **ما الذي فعلوه فعلاً بأموالهم** — والسلوك هو عادة أقوى مؤشر على ما سيفعلونه بعد ذلك.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: يمكن لشخصين يبلغان 34 سنة في Austin بدخل متطابق ألا يكون لديهما شيء مشترك كعملاء؛ أحدهما يشتري نفس العلامة التجارية لمدة عقد، والآخر يتبدل في كل مرة يكون هناك كوبون.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: المشكلة: من الصعب ملاحظة السلوك *قبل* أن يصبح شخص ما عميلاً.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: لذا فإن سير العمل الشائع هو **التقسيم حسب السلوك والاحتياجات، ثم تحديد الملف الشخصي بالديموغرافيات** — لأن الديموغرافيات هي ما تتيح لك العثور على هؤلاء الأشخاص فعلاً في منصة إعلانات أو قائمة بريدية أو قرار موقع متجر.

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### متى يكون القطاع يستحق امتلاكه؟

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: ليس كل مجموعة يمكنك تسميتها هي قطاع يستحق المتابعة.

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: قائمة المراجعة القياسية:

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **قابل للقياس** — يمكنك تحديد حجمه ووصفه.

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **كبير** — كبير بما يكفي ليستحق الجهد.

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **يمكن الوصول إليه** — يمكنك فعلاً الوصول إليه من خلال الوسائط والتوزيع.

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **قابل للتفريق** — يستجيب لعرضك بشكل مختلف عن القطاعات الأخرى. (هذا ما يتخطاه الناس، وهو ما يجعل التقسيم *تقسيماً* بدلاً من التفاهات.)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **قابل للتنفيذ** — لديك الموارد لخدمته بشكل جيد.

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: طريقة تقريبية لتحديد حجم واحد، بحسابات بسيطة:

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: ثم اطرح ما يكلفه الوصول إليهم وخدمتهم.

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: القطاع الضخم الذي لا يمكنك الوصول إليه برخصة يستحق أقل من القطاع الصغير الذي من السهل العثور عليه.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية: هرعة الصالة الرياضية في يناير

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: في كل يناير، تقريباً نفس القرار — "الحصول على لياقة بدنية" — يرسل ملايين الأمريكيين يبحثون عن صالة رياضية.

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: من الخارج، يبدو أنه سوق واحد.

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: إنها أربع على الأقل.

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness** تبيع عضوية Classic بحوالي $15 شهرياً، وتلف المكان بالأرجواني والأصفر، وتسميه "منطقة خالية من الحكم".

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: هذه الشعار ليست ديكور — إنها ضربة نفسية موجهة للأشخاص الذين *يريدون* ممارسة الرياضة ولكنهم يشعرون بالخجل من المشي بجانب صف من رافعي الأثقال.

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: لاحظ زاوية السلوك أيضاً: يعمل سعر منخفض جداً عبر قاعدة أعضاء كبيرة جداً بالضبط لأن متوسط العضو لا يظهر كثيراً.

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: المستخدمون الخفيفون هم، بشكل غير عادي، الأرباح.

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox** تفرض رسوماً تزيد عن $200 شهرياً في الأسواق الرئيسية وقد أطلقت حملة قالت "نحن لا نتحدث الرياضة".

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: نفس الفئة العريضة، القطاع المعاكس: أشخاص يكون النادي بالنسبة لهم سلعة حالة وإشارة نمط حياة، وليس بند لتقليله.

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **صالة CrossFit** عادة ما تكلف $150–$250 شهرياً مقابل شيء لا تبيعه Planet Fitness عن قصد — مدرب يعرف اسمك وفصل الساعة 6 صباحاً.

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: يلاحظ عندما تكون غائباً.

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: الفائدة المطلوبة هي المساءلة والمجتمع.

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **المشتري في المنزل** — Peloton، مجموعة من الأوزان القابلة للتعديل، اشتراك YouTube — غالباً ما يتم تقسيمه حسب مرحلة الحياة أكثر من الدخل: والد يعنى بأطفال صغار لا يستطيعون حرفياً مغادرة المنزل الساعة 6 صباحاً.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: الآن الجزء المهم.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: لا تخسر Equinox أمام Planet Fitness.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: هم بالكاد في نفس المعركة.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: بنى كل منها منتجاً وسعراً واستراتيجية موقع ونبرة صوت حول مجموعة تتصرف بشكل مختلف — وسيضر كل منها بنفسه محاولاً الفوز على الآخرين.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: ستدمر Equinox بـ $15 إشارتها الخاصة.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: ستنفجر Planet Fitness مع مدربين شخصيين في كل زاوية من هيكل التكلفة الخاص بها وتخيف الأشخاص بالضبط الذين تم بناؤها من أجلهم.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: هذا هو التقسيم يقوم بوظيفته: ليس وصف العملاء، بل *تقرير ما أنت على استعداد أن تكون سيئاً فيه*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص 3 أسطر

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. التقسيم ينقسم سوق عريض إلى مجموعات تستجيب بشكل مختلف — إنها الخطوة الأولى من STP، و "الجميع" ليس قطاعاً.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. القواعد الأربع هي الجغرافية والديموغرافية والنفسية والسلوكية؛ يتنبأ السلوك بشكل أفضل، وتصل الديموغرافيات إلى الأفضل، لذا يقسم معظم المسوقين حسب السلوك وينشئ الملف الشخصي مع الديموغرافيات.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. القطاع يستحق الخدمة فقط إذا كان قابلاً للقياس وكبيراً ويمكن الوصول إليه وقابلاً للتفريق وقابلاً للتنفيذ — اختبار التفريق هو ما يفصل القطاعات الحقيقية عن التفاهات.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a **behavioral** segmentation variable?
segments.tr: **Q1.** أي من هذه متغيرات تقسيم **سلوكية**؟

segments.src: a) Household income
segments.tr: a) دخل الأسرة

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) مناسبة الشراء (على سبيل المثال، شراء الزهور ليوم الأم)

segments.src: c) ZIP code
segments.tr: c) الرمز البريدي

segments.src: d) Age
segments.tr: d) العمر

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A segment of 40 million Americans who all say they want a product is automatically an attractive segment to target.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) قطاع من 40 مليون أمريكي يقولون جميعاً أنهم يريدون منتجاً هو تلقائياً قطاعاً جذاباً للاستهداف.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gym brands itself a "Judgement Free Zone" to appeal to people who feel intimidated by traditional gyms.
segments.tr: **Q3.** تعلّم صالة رياضية نفسها "منطقة خالية من الحكم" لاستقطاب الأشخاص الذين يشعرون بالخوف من صالات الرياضة التقليدية.

segments.src: This is primarily which kind of segmentation?
segments.tr: هذا أساساً أي نوع من التقسيم؟

segments.src: a) Geographic
segments.tr: a) جغرافي

segments.src: b) Demographic
segments.tr: b) ديموغرافي

segments.src: c) Psychographic
segments.tr: c) نفسي

segments.src: d) Loyalty-based
segments.tr: d) قائم على الولاء

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Market segmentation** — Dividing a broad market into subgroups that are internally similar and behave differently from one another in ways that affect buying.
segments.tr: - **تقسيم السوق** — تقسيم سوق عريض إلى مجموعات فرعية تكون متشابهة داخلياً وتتصرف بشكل مختلف عن بعضها البعض بطرق تؤثر على الشراء.

segments.src: - **Segmentation base** — The variable you cut the market on (age, region, usage rate, values, and so on).
segments.tr: - **قاعدة التقسيم** — المتغير الذي تقطع السوق عليه (العمر والمنطقة ومعدل الاستخدام والقيم وما إلى ذلك).

segments.src: - **Demographic segmentation** — Grouping by observable population traits: age, income, gender, household size, life stage.
segments.tr: - **التقسيم الديموغرافي** — التجميع حسب خصائص السكان الملحوظة: العمر والدخل والجنس وحجم الأسرة ومرحلة الحياة.
