fr.title: [Marketing 101 #5] Pourquoi « Tout le monde » est le pire client que vous pouvez poursuivre

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > La segmentation du marché est l'acte de découper un large marché en groupes de personnes qui se comportent différemment — afin que vous puissiez arrêter de crier à tout le monde et commencer à parler à quelqu'un.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: Demandez à un créateur novice qui est son client, et vous entendrez souvent : « Honnêtement ?

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: Quiconque en a besoin."

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: Cette réponse semble ambitieuse.

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: C'est en fait la phrase la plus coûteuse en affaires.

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: Si votre client est tout le monde, alors votre annonce doit plaire à tout le monde, votre prix doit fonctionner pour tout le monde, et votre produit doit être un peu juste pour tout le monde — ce qui signifie généralement qu'il n'est exactement juste pour personne.

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **La segmentation du marché** est la solution.

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: C'est le processus de division d'un marché en sous-groupes dont les membres se ressemblent et diffèrent des autres groupes d'une manière qui *importe pour le comportement d'achat*.

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: C'est le « S » dans la séquence STP classique : **Segmentation → Ciblage → Positionnement**.

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: Segmentez d'abord (comment ce marché se divise-t-il naturellement ?), puis choisissez les tranches à servir, puis décidez ce que vous représenterez pour eux.

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: Une chose qui confond les gens : vous ne *créez* pas les segments.

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: Vous les *découvrez*.

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: Les différences sont déjà là, dans les portefeuilles et les calendriers des gens.

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: Votre travail consiste à trouver les lignes de coupure qui sont réelles.

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### Les quatre familles de variables de segmentation

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: Les responsables marketing divisent les marchés en utilisant quatre grands types de **bases** (les variables sur lesquelles vous coupez) :

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **Géographique** — région, climat, ville ou banlieue, code postal. Les souffleurs de neige se vendent différemment à Minneapolis qu'à Phoenix.

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **Démographique** — âge, revenu, sexe, taille du ménage, éducation, étape de la vie. Facile à mesurer, facile à cibler via les médias.

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **Psychographique** — valeurs, mode de vie, personnalité, image de soi, identité. *Pourquoi* quelqu'un achète.

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **Comportemental** — taux d'utilisation, occasion d'achat, avantages recherchés, statut de fidélité, sensibilité aux prix. *Ce qu'ils font réellement.*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: Voici la hiérarchie pratique que la plupart des responsables marketing expérimentés adoptent.

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: Les données démographiques vous disent **qui**.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: Les données psychographiques vous disent **pourquoi**.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: Le comportement vous dit **ce qu'ils ont réellement fait avec leur argent** — et le comportement est généralement le meilleur prédicteur de ce qu'ils feront ensuite.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: Deux personnes de 34 ans à Austin avec des revenus identiques peuvent n'avoir rien en commun en tant que clients ; l'une achète la même marque pendant une décennie, l'autre change chaque fois qu'il y a une promotion.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: Le hic : le comportement est difficile à observer *avant* que quelqu'un ne devienne client.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: Ainsi, le flux de travail courant consiste à **segmenter selon le comportement et les besoins, puis profiler avec les données démographiques** — car ce sont les données démographiques qui vous permettent de trouver réellement ces personnes sur une plateforme publicitaire, une liste de diffusion ou une décision de localisation de magasin.

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### Quand un segment vaut-il la peine d'être retenu ?

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: Chaque groupe que vous pouvez nommer n'est pas un segment qui vaut la peine d'être poursuivi.

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: La liste de contrôle standard :

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **Mesurable** — vous pouvez le dimensionner et le décrire.

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **Substantiel** — assez grand pour justifier l'effort.

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **Accessible** — vous pouvez réellement l'atteindre avec des médias et de la distribution.

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **Différentiable** — il répond à votre offre différemment que les autres segments. (C'est celui que les gens sautent, et c'est celui qui fait que la segmentation *est* la segmentation plutôt que de la trivialité.)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **Exploitable** — vous disposez des ressources pour le servir correctement.

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: Une manière approximative d'en dimensionner un, en arithmétique simple :

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: Puis soustrayez le coût de les atteindre et de les servir.

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: Un énorme segment que vous ne pouvez pas atteindre à bon marché vaut moins qu'un petit qui est facile à trouver.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne : la ruée des gymnases de janvier

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: Chaque janvier, à peu près la même résolution — « se mettre en forme » — envoie des millions d'Américains à la recherche d'une salle de sport.

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: De l'extérieur, cela ressemble à un seul marché.

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: C'est au moins quatre.

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness** vend un abonnement Classic pour environ 15 $ par mois, enveloppe l'endroit de violet et de jaune, et l'appelle une « Zone sans jugement ».

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: Ce slogan n'est pas une décoration — c'est une cible psychographique visant les gens qui *veulent* faire de l'exercice mais se sentent mal à l'aise en passant devant d'imposants powerlifters.

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: Remarquez aussi l'angle comportemental : un prix très bas sur une très grande base de membres fonctionne précisément parce que le membre moyen ne se montre pas souvent.

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: Les utilisateurs occasionnels sont, fait curieusement, les plus rentables.

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox** facture bien plus de 200 $ par mois sur les grands marchés et, célèbrement, a une fois lancé une campagne qui disait « Nous ne parlons pas de gym ».

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: Même grande catégorie, segment opposé : les personnes pour lesquelles le club est un bien de statut et un signal de mode de vie, pas un simple poste budgétaire à minimiser.

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **Une box CrossFit** coûte généralement entre 150 et 250 $ par mois pour quelque chose que Planet Fitness ne vend délibérément pas — un entraîneur qui connaît votre nom et une classe de 6 h du matin.

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: qui remarque quand vous manquez.

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: L'avantage recherché est l'imputabilité et la communauté.

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **L'acheteur à domicile** — Peloton, un ensemble d'haltères réglables, un abonnement YouTube — est souvent segmenté par étape de la vie plutôt que par revenu : un parent avec de jeunes enfants qui ne peut littéralement pas quitter la maison à 6 h du matin.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: Maintenant, la partie importante.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox ne perd pas contre Planet Fitness.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: Ils sont à peine dans le même combat.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: Chacun a construit un produit, un prix, une stratégie de localisation et un ton de voix autour d'un groupe qui se comporte différemment — et chacun s'endommagerait en essayant de surpasser les autres.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: Un Equinox à 15 $ détruirait son propre signal.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: Un Planet Fitness avec des entraîneurs personnels à chaque coin détruirait sa structure de coûts et effraierait précisément les gens pour lesquels il a été conçu.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: C'est cela que la segmentation fait : non pas décrire les clients, mais *décider ce dans quoi vous êtes prêt à être mauvais*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. La segmentation divise un large marché en groupes qui réagissent différemment — c'est la première étape de STP, et « tout le monde » n'est pas un segment.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. Les quatre bases sont géographique, démographique, psychographique et comportementale ; le comportement prédit le mieux, la démographie atteint le mieux, donc la plupart des responsables marketing segmentent selon le comportement et se servent des données démographiques pour profiler.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. Un segment ne vaut la peine d'être servi que s'il est mesurable, substantiel, accessible, différentiable et exploitable — le test de différentiabilité est celui qui sépare les vrais segments de la trivialité.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Auto-test

segments.tr: **Q1.** Lequel de ceux-ci est une variable de segmentation **comportementale** ?

segments.tr: a) Revenu du ménage

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) Occasion d'achat (par exemple, acheter des fleurs pour la fête des mères)

segments.tr: d) Âge

segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) Un segment de 40 millions d'Américains qui disent tous qu'ils veulent un produit est automatiquement un segment attrayant à cibler.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gym brands itself a "Judgement Free Zone" to appeal to people who feel intimidated by traditional gyms.
segments.tr: **Q3.** Une salle de sport se présente comme une « Zone sans jugement » pour plaire aux personnes qui se sentent intimidées par les salles de sport traditionnelles.

segments.tr: Dados demográficos dizem **quem**.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: Psicográficos dizem **por quê**.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: O comportamento diz **o que eles realmente fizeram com seu dinheiro** — e o comportamento é geralmente o melhor preditor do que eles farão em seguida.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: Duas pessoas de 34 anos em Austin com renda idêntica podem não ter nada em comum como clientes; uma compra a mesma marca por uma década, a outra muda toda vez que há um cupom.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: O detalhe: o comportamento é difícil de observar *antes* de alguém se tornar cliente.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: Então o fluxo de trabalho comum é **segmentar por comportamento e necessidades, depois fazer perfil com dados demográficos** — porque dados demográficos são o que permite encontrar essas pessoas em uma plataforma de publicidade, uma lista de e-mail ou uma decisão de localização de loja.

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### Quando um segmento vale a pena ter?

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: Nem todo grupo que você pode nomear é um segmento que vale a pena perseguir.

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: A lista de verificação padrão:

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **Mensurável** — você pode dimensioná-lo e descrevê-lo.

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **Substancial** — grande o suficiente para valer o esforço.

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **Acessível** — você realmente pode alcançá-lo com mídia e distribuição.

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **Diferenciável** — responde à sua oferta de forma diferente de outros segmentos. (Este é o que as pessoas pulam, e é o que torna a segmentação *segmentação* em vez de trivialidade.)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **Acionável** — você tem os recursos para servi-lo bem.

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: Uma maneira aproximada de dimensionar um, em aritmética simples:

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: Depois subtraia o custo de alcançá-los e servi-los.

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: Um segmento enorme que você não pode alcançar com preço acessível vale menos do que um pequeno que é fácil de encontrar.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Cotidiana: A Correria de Academia de Janeiro

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: A cada janeiro, aproximadamente a mesma resolução — "ficar em forma" — envia milhões de americanos em busca de uma academia.

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: De fora parece um mercado.

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: São pelo menos quatro.

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness** vende uma associação Classic por cerca de $15 por mês, envolve o lugar em roxo e amarelo, e a chama de "Zona Livre de Julgamento".

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: Esse slogan não é decoração — é um alvo psicográfico direto a pessoas que *querem* se exercitar mas se sentem constrangidas passando por uma fileira de levantadores de peso grunhindo.

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: Observe também o ângulo comportamental: um preço muito baixo em uma base de membros muito grande funciona precisamente porque o membro médio não aparece com frequência.

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: Usuários leves são, inusualmente, os lucrativos.

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox** cobra bem acima de $200 por mês em principais mercados e, famosamente, uma vez dirigiu uma campanha que dizia "Não falamos academia".

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: Mesma categoria ampla, segmento oposto: pessoas para quem o clube é um bem de status e um sinal de estilo de vida, não um item de linha para minimizar.

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **Uma box de CrossFit** geralmente custa $150–$250 por mês por algo que Planet Fitness deliberadamente não vende — um treinador que conhece seu nome e uma aula das 6 da manhã

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: que percebe quando você não aparece.

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: O benefício procurado é responsabilidade e comunidade.

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **O comprador em casa** — Peloton, um conjunto de halteres ajustáveis, uma assinatura do YouTube — é frequentemente segmentado por estágio de vida mais do que renda: um pai com filhos pequenos que literalmente não pode sair de casa às 6 da manhã.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: Agora a parte importante.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox não está perdendo para Planet Fitness.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: Eles estão mal na mesma luta.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: Cada um construiu um produto, um preço, uma estratégia de localização e um tom de voz em torno de um grupo que se comporta diferentemente — e cada um se danificaria tentando vencer os outros.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: Um Equinox de $15 destruiria seu próprio sinal.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: Um Planet Fitness com treinadores pessoais em cada canto explodiria sua estrutura de custos e assustaria exatamente as pessoas para as quais foi construído.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: Essa é a segmentação fazendo seu trabalho: não descrevendo clientes, mas *decidindo no que você está disposto a ser ruim*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 Linhas

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. Segmentação divide um mercado amplo em grupos que respondem diferentemente — é o primeiro passo do STP, e "todos" não é um segmento.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. As quatro bases são geográfica, demográfica, psicográfica e comportamental; comportamento prediz melhor, dados demográficos alcançam melhor, então a maioria dos profissionais de marketing segmenta por comportamento e perfila com dados demográficos.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. Um segmento só vale a pena servir se for mensurável, substancial, acessível, diferenciável e acionável — o teste diferenciável é o que separa segmentos reais de trivialidades.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Market segmentation** — Dividing a broad market into subgroups that are internally similar and behave differently from one another in ways that affect buying.
segments.tr: - **Segmentação de mercado** — Dividir um mercado amplo em subgrupos que são internamente semelhantes e se comportam diferentemente um do outro de maneiras que afetam a compra.

segments.src: - **Segmentation base** — The variable you cut the market on (age, region, usage rate, values, and so on).
segments.tr: - **Base de segmentação** — A variável que você usa para cortar o mercado (idade, região, taxa de uso, valores, e assim por diante).

segments.src: - **Demographic segmentation** — Grouping by observable population traits: age, income, gender, household size, life stage.
segments.tr: - **Segmentação demográfica** — Agrupamento por características populacionais observáveis: idade, renda, gênero, tamanho familiar, estágio de vida.

segments.src: - **Psychographic segmentation** — Grouping by values, lifestyle, personality, and self-image — the *why* behind a purchase.
segments.tr: - **Segmentação psicográfica** — Agrupamento por valores, estilo de vida, personalidade e autoimagem — o *por quê* por trás de uma compra.

segments.src: - **Behavioral segmentation** — Grouping by what people actually do: how often they buy, on what occasion, which benefit they're after, how loyal or price-sensitive they are.
segments.tr: - **Segmentação comportamental** — Agrupamento pelo que as pessoas realmente fazem: com que frequência compram, em que ocasião, qual benefício buscam, quão leais ou sensíveis ao preço são.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — b.** Occasion is about buying behavior; income, ZIP code, and age are demographic or geographic descriptors.
segments.tr: *Respostas: **Q1 — b.** Ocasião é sobre comportamento de compra; renda, código postal e idade são descritores demográficos ou geográficos.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** Size is only one of five tests.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (falso).** Tamanho é apenas um de cinco testes.

segments.src: A giant segment that you can't reach affordably, that doesn't respond differently to your offer, or that you lack the resources to serve is not attractive — "substantial" without "accessible," "differentiable," and "actionable" is a trap.
segments.tr: Um segmento gigante que você não pode alcançar com preço acessível, que não responde diferentemente à sua oferta, ou para o qual você não tem recursos para servir não é atraente — "substancial" sem "acessível", "diferenciável" e "acionável" é uma armadilha.

segments.src: **Q3 — c.** It targets a feeling and self-image (exercise anxiety, not wanting to be watched), which is psychographic — even though the brand will then use demographics like age and income to find those people in ad platforms.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — c.** Ela direciona um sentimento e autoimagem (ansiedade de exercício, não querer ser observado), que é psicográfico — embora a marca então use dados demográficos como idade e renda para encontrar essas pessoas em plataformas de publicidade.*

in.title: [Marketing 101 #5] Mengapa "Semua Orang" Adalah Pelanggan Terburuk yang Bisa Anda Kejar

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > Segmentasi pasar adalah tindakan membagi pasar yang luas menjadi kelompok orang yang berperilaku berbeda — sehingga Anda dapat berhenti berteriak kepada semua orang dan mulai berbicara kepada seseorang.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: Tanyakan kepada pendiri pemula siapa pelanggan mereka, dan Anda sering mendengar: "Jujur?

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: Siapa saja yang membutuhkan ini."

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: Jawaban itu terasa ambisius.

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: Sebenarnya itu kalimat paling mahal dalam bisnis.

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: Jika pelanggan Anda adalah semua orang, maka iklan Anda harus menarik bagi semua orang, harga Anda harus berlaku untuk semua orang, dan produk Anda harus sedikit tepat untuk semua orang — yang biasanya berarti itu tepat untuk tidak ada siapa pun.

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **Segmentasi pasar** adalah solusinya.

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: Ini adalah proses membagi pasar menjadi subkelompok yang anggotanya mirip satu sama lain dan berbeda dari kelompok lain dalam cara yang *penting untuk perilaku pembelian*.

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: Ini adalah "S" dalam urutan STP klasik: **Segmentasi → Penargetan → Positioning**.

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: Segmentasi terlebih dahulu (bagaimana pasar ini terbagi secara alami?), kemudian pilih irisan mana yang akan dilayani, kemudian tentukan apa yang akan Anda maksudkan bagi mereka.

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: Satu hal yang membuat orang terpeleset: Anda tidak *membuat* segmen.

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: Anda *menemukannya*.

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: Perbedaannya sudah ada di dompet dan kalender orang-orang.

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: Pekerjaan Anda adalah menemukan garis potong yang nyata.

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### Empat keluarga variabel segmentasi

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: Pemasar memotong pasar menggunakan empat jenis **basis** yang luas (variabel yang Anda potong):

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **Geografis** — wilayah, iklim, kota vs. pinggiran, kode ZIP. Pengering salju terjual berbeda di Minneapolis dibanding di Phoenix.

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **Demografis** — usia, pendapatan, jenis kelamin, ukuran rumah tangga, pendidikan, tahap kehidupan. Mudah diukur, mudah membeli media melawannya.

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **Psikografis** — nilai, gaya hidup, kepribadian, citra diri, identitas. *Mengapa* seseorang membeli.

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **Perilaku** — tingkat penggunaan, kesempatan pembelian, manfaat yang dicari, status loyalitas, sensitivitas harga. *Apa yang sebenarnya mereka lakukan.*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: Berikut adalah hierarki praktis yang disepakati oleh sebagian besar pemasar berpengalaman.

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: Demografis memberitahu Anda **siapa**.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: Psikografis memberitahu Anda **mengapa**.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: Perilaku memberitahu Anda **apa yang sebenarnya mereka lakukan dengan uang mereka** — dan perilaku biasanya merupakan prediktor terkuat dari apa yang akan mereka lakukan selanjutnya.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: Dua orang berusia 34 tahun di Austin dengan pendapatan yang identik mungkin tidak memiliki apa pun yang sama sebagai pelanggan; yang satu membeli merek yang sama selama satu dekade, yang lain beralih setiap kali ada kupon.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: Tangkapannya: perilaku sulit untuk diamati *sebelum* seseorang menjadi pelanggan.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: Jadi alur kerja umum adalah **segmen berdasarkan perilaku dan kebutuhan, kemudian profil dengan demografis** — karena demografis adalah apa yang memungkinkan Anda benar-benar menemukan orang-orang ini di platform iklan, daftar surat, atau keputusan lokasi toko.

segments.tr: **Pembeli di rumah** — Peloton, satu set dumbel yang dapat disesuaikan, langganan YouTube — sering disegmentasikan berdasarkan tahap kehidupan lebih dari pendapatan: orang tua dengan anak kecil yang benar-benar tidak bisa meninggalkan rumah pukul 6 pagi.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: Sekarang bagian yang penting.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox tidak kalah dari Planet Fitness.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: Mereka hampir tidak dalam pertarungan yang sama.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: Masing-masing membangun produk, harga, strategi lokasi, dan nada suara di sekitar kelompok yang berperilaku berbeda — dan masing-masing akan merusak dirinya sendiri mencoba untuk memenangkan yang lain.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: Equinox $15 akan menghancurkan sinyal miliknya sendiri.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: Planet Fitness dengan pelatih pribadi di setiap sudut akan meledakkan struktur biayanya dan menakut-nakuti orang-orang yang tepat yang dibangun untuknya.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: Itu adalah segmentasi yang melakukan tugasnya: bukan menjelaskan pelanggan, tetapi *memutuskan apa yang bersedia Anda jelek*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan 3 Baris

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. Segmentasi membagi pasar yang luas menjadi kelompok yang merespons secara berbeda — ini adalah langkah pertama STP, dan "semua orang" bukan segmen.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. Empat basis adalah geografis, demografis, psikografis, dan perilaku; perilaku memprediksi terbaik, demografis mencapai terbaik, jadi sebagian besar pemasar segmen pada perilaku dan profil dengan demografis.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. Segmen hanya layak dilayani jika dapat diukur, substansial, dapat diakses, dapat dibedakan, dan dapat ditindaklanjuti — tes yang dapat dibedakan adalah yang memisahkan segmen nyata dari trivia.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a **behavioral** segmentation variable?
segments.tr: **Q1.** Manakah dari ini yang merupakan variabel segmentasi **perilaku**?

segments.src: a) Household income
segments.tr: a) Pendapatan rumah tangga

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) Kesempatan pembelian (misalnya, membeli bunga untuk Hari Ibu)

segments.src: c) ZIP code
segments.tr: c) Kode ZIP

segments.src: d) Age
segments.tr: d) Usia

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A segment of 40 million Americans who all say they want a product is automatically an attractive segment to target.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) Segmen 40 juta orang Amerika yang semuanya mengatakan mereka menginginkan produk secara otomatis adalah segmen yang menarik untuk ditargetkan.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gym brands itself a "Judgement Free Zone" to appeal to people who feel intimidated by traditional gyms.
segments.tr: **Q3.** Gym merek dirinya "Zona Bebas Penilaian" untuk menarik orang-orang yang merasa ditakut-takuti oleh gym tradisional.

segments.src: This is primarily which kind of segmentation?
segments.tr: Ini terutama adalah segmentasi apa?

segments.src: a) Geographic
segments.tr: a) Geografis

segments.src: b) Demographic
segments.tr: b) Demografis

segments.tr: c) Psikografis

segments.src: d) Loyalty-based
segments.tr: d) Berbasis loyalitas

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Market segmentation** — Dividing a broad market into subgroups that are internally similar and behave differently from one another in ways that affect buying.
segments.tr: - **Segmentasi pasar** — Membagi pasar yang luas menjadi subkelompok yang mirip secara internal dan berperilaku berbeda satu sama lain dalam cara yang mempengaruhi pembelian.

segments.src: - **Segmentation base** — The variable you cut the market on (age, region, usage rate, values, and so on).
segments.tr: - **Basis segmentasi** — Variabel yang Anda potong pasarnya (usia, wilayah, tingkat penggunaan, nilai, dan seterusnya).

segments.src: - **Demographic segmentation** — Grouping by observable population traits: age, income, gender, household size, life stage.
segments.tr: - **Segmentasi demografis** — Pengelompokan berdasarkan sifat populasi yang dapat diamati: usia, pendapatan, jenis kelamin, ukuran rumah tangga, tahap kehidupan.

segments.src: - **Psychographic segmentation** — Grouping by values, lifestyle, personality, and self-image — the *why* behind a purchase.
segments.tr: - **Segmentasi psikografis** — Pengelompokan berdasarkan nilai, gaya hidup, kepribadian, dan citra diri — *mengapa* di balik pembelian.

segments.src: - **Behavioral segmentation** — Grouping by what people actually do: how often they buy, on what occasion, which benefit they're after, how loyal or price-sensitive they are.
segments.tr: - **Segmentasi perilaku** — Pengelompokan berdasarkan apa yang sebenarnya orang lakukan: seberapa sering mereka membeli, pada kesempatan apa, manfaat apa yang mereka kejar, betapa loyal atau sensitif harga mereka.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — b.** Occasion is about buying behavior; income, ZIP code, and age are demographic or geographic descriptors.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — b.** Kesempatan adalah tentang perilaku pembelian; pendapatan, kode ZIP, dan usia adalah deskriptor demografis atau geografis.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** Size is only one of five tests.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (salah).** Ukuran hanya satu dari lima tes.

segments.src: A giant segment that you can't reach affordably, that doesn't respond differently to your offer, or that you lack the resources to serve is not attractive — "substantial" without "accessible," "differentiable," and "actionable" is a trap.
segments.tr: Segmen raksasa yang tidak bisa Anda jangkau dengan terjangkau, yang tidak merespons berbeda dengan penawaran Anda, atau yang Anda kurang sumber daya untuk melayani tidaklah menarik — "substansial" tanpa "dapat diakses," "dapat dibedakan," dan "dapat ditindaklanjuti" adalah jebakan.

segments.src: **Q3 — c.** It targets a feeling and self-image (exercise anxiety, not wanting to be watched), which is psychographic — even though the brand will then use demographics like age and income to find those people in ad platforms.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — c.** Itu menargetkan perasaan dan citra diri (kecemasan olahraga, tidak ingin ditonton), yang psikografis — meskipun merek kemudian akan menggunakan demografis seperti usia dan pendapatan untuk menemukan orang-orang itu di platform iklan.*

ja.title: [マーケティング 101 #5] なぜ「誰もが」最悪の顧客ターゲットなのか

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > マーケットセグメンテーションは、幅広い市場を異なる行動をする人々のグループに分割する行為です。そうすることで、万人に叫びかけるのをやめて、特定の誰かに話しかけることができるのです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: 初めての起業家に顧客が誰かを聞くと、多くの場合このような答えが返ってきます：「正直に言うと？

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: これが必要な誰もが。"

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: その答えは野心的に聞こえます。

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: それは実はビジネスで最も高くつく文句です。

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: 顧客が万人であれば、広告は万人に訴える必要があり、価格は万人に機能する必要があり、製品は万人に少しは正しくなければなりません。これは通常、誰にも全く正しくないことを意味します。

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **マーケットセグメンテーション**がその解決策です。

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: これは市場をサブグループに分割するプロセスであり、各グループのメンバーは互いに類似しており、*購買行動に影響を与える*方法で他のグループと異なっています。

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: これは古典的なSTPシーケンスの「S」です：**セグメンテーション → ターゲティング → ポジショニング**。

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: まずセグメント化し（この市場はどのように自然に分割されますか？）、次にどのスライスをサービスするかを選択し、それからそれらにとってあなたが何を意味するかを決めます。

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: 人々を戸惑わせることの1つは、セグメントを*作成する*わけではないということです。

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: あなたはそれを*発見*するのです。

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: その差は既に人々の財布とカレンダーに存在しています。

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: あなたの仕事は、実際に存在する分割線を見つけることです。

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### セグメンテーション変数の4つのファミリー

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: マーケターは4つの広いカテゴリーの**ベース**（分割変数）を使って市場を分割します：

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **地理的** — 地域、気候、都市 vs. 郊外、郵便番号。除雪機はミネアポリスではフェニックスとは異なる売れ方をします。

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **人口統計学的** — 年齢、収入、性別、世帯規模、教育、人生段階。測定しやすく、メディア購入がしやすい。

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **心理的** — 価値観、ライフスタイル、パーソナリティ、自己イメージ、アイデンティティ。 *なぜ*誰かが購入するか。

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **行動的** — 使用率、購買機会、求める利益、ロイヤルティステータス、価格感度。 *彼らが実際に行うこと。*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: これが最も経験豊富なマーケターが到達する実用的な階層です。

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: 人口統計学的データは**誰が**かを教えてくれます。

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: 心理的データは**なぜ**かを教えてくれます。

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: 行動は**彼らが実際にお金で何をしたか**を教えてくれます。行動は通常、彼らが次に何をするかの最強の予測因子です。

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: 同じ収入を持つオースティンの2人の34歳は、顧客として何も共通点がないかもしれません。1人は10年間同じブランドを買い続け、もう1人はクーポンが出るたびに切り替えます。

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: 問題は、誰かが顧客になる*前に*行動を観察するのは難しいということです。

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: ですから、一般的なワークフローは**行動とニーズでセグメント化して、次に人口統計学的データでプロファイルする**ことです。人口統計学的データは、広告プラットフォーム、メーリングリスト、または店舗ロケーション決定でこれらの人々を実際に見つけることができるからです。

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### セグメントを持つ価値があるのはいつですか？

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: 名前を付けることができるすべてのグループが追求する価値のあるセグメントではありません。

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: 標準チェックリスト：

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **測定可能** — サイズを決定し、説明することができます。

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **実質的** — 努力する価値があるほど十分に大きい。

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **アクセス可能** — メディアと流通で実際にそれに到達できます。

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **差別化可能** — 他のセグメントとは異なり、あなたのオファーに応答します。（これは人々がスキップするものであり、セグメンテーションを雑学ではなく*セグメンテーション*にするものです。）

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **実行可能** — それをよくサービスするためのリソースがあります。

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: 1つのサイズを推定する単純な算術的な方法：

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: 次に、それらに到達してサービスするのにかかるコストを差し引きます。

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: 安く到達できない巨大なセグメントは、見つけやすい小さなセグメントより価値が低いです。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で：1月のジム殺到

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: 毎年1月、ほぼ同じ決意—「体を鍛える」—がアメリカ人の何百万人もがジムを探すように促します。

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: 外からは1つの市場に見えます。

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: それは少なくとも4つです。

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness**は月約$15のClassicメンバーシップを販売し、場所を紫と黄色でラップし、「判断なしゾーン」と呼んでいます。

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: そのタグラインは装飾ではなく、うなり声をあげるパワーリフターの列を歩くことに自意識を感じる、*運動したい*人を狙った心理的な的です。

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: 行動的な角度にも注目してください。非常に低い価格が非常に大きなメンバーベース全体で機能するのは、平均的なメンバーがそれほど頻繁に現れないためです。

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: ライトユーザーは、珍しいことに、利益をもたらす者です。

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox**は主要市場で月$200以上を請求し、有名なことに、「We don't speak gym」と言うキャンペーンを実行しました。

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: 同じ広いカテゴリ、反対セグメント：クラブが最小化するライン項目ではなく、ステータス商品とライフスタイル信号である人々。

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **CrossFitボックス**は通常、Planet Fitnessが意図的に販売していないものに月$150～$250かかります—あなたの名前を知っているコーチと午前6時。

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: あなたが欠席していることに気づくクラス。

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: 求められる利益は説明責任とコミュニティです。

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **自宅購入者** — Peloton、調整可能なダンベルのセット、YouTubeサブスクリプション — は収入よりも人生段階でセグメント化されることが多いです。文字通り午前6時に家を出ることができない小さな子供を持つ親。

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: ここで重要な部分です。

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: EquinoxはPlanet Fitnessに負けていません。

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: 彼らはほぼ同じ戦いに参加していません。

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: それぞれが異なる行動をする集団を中心に製品、価格、ロケーション戦略、声のトーンを構築しました。そして、他を打ち負かそうとすることで、それぞれが自分自身に損害を与えるでしょう。

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: $15のEquinoxは独自の信号を破壊するでしょう。

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: すべての角にパーソナルコーチがいるPlanet Fitnessは、そのコスト構造を爆発させ、それが作られた正確な人々を追い払うでしょう。

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: それはセグメンテーションがその仕事をしているのです。顧客を説明するのではなく、*あなたが悪いことに喜んで受け入れる準備ができていることを決めること*。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行のまとめ

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. セグメンテーションは幅広い市場を異なる応答をするグループに分割します。これはSTPの最初のステップであり、「万人」はセグメントではありません。

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. 4つのベースは地理的、人口統計学的、心理的、行動的です。行動が最も良く予測し、人口統計学的データが最も良く到達するため、ほとんどのマーケターは行動でセグメント化して、人口統計学的データでプロファイルします。

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. セグメントは、測定可能、実質的、アクセス可能、差別化可能、実行可能である場合にのみサービスする価値があります。差別化テストは、実際のセグメントを雑学から分離するものです。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ セルフクイズ

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a **behavioral** segmentation variable?
segments.tr: **Q1.**これらのうち、どれが**行動的**セグメンテーション変数ですか？

segments.src: a) Household income
segments.tr: a) 世帯収入

segments.src: b) Purchase occasion (e.g., buying flowers for Mother's Day)
segments.tr: b) 購買機会（例えば、母の日に花を買う）

segments.src: c) ZIP code
segments.tr: c) 郵便番号

segments.src: d) Age
segments.tr: d) 年齢

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) A segment of 40 million Americans who all say they want a product is automatically an attractive segment to target.
segments.tr: **Q2.**（〇/✕）製品が欲しいと言う4,000万人のアメリカ人のセグメントは、自動的に対象にする魅力的なセグメントです。

de.title: [Marketing 101 #5] Warum "Jeder" der schlimmste Kunde ist, den Sie verfolgen können

segments.src: > Market segmentation is the act of cutting a broad market into groups of people who behave differently — so you can stop shouting at everyone and start speaking to someone.
segments.tr: > Marktsegmentierung ist das Aufteilen eines großen Marktes in Gruppen von Menschen, die sich unterschiedlich verhalten — damit Sie aufhören können, an alle zu schreien, und anfangen können, mit jemandem zu sprechen.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Ask a first-time founder who their customer is, and you'll often hear: "Honestly?
segments.tr: Fragen Sie einen Gründer zum ersten Mal, wer sein Kunde ist, und Sie werden oft hören: "Ehrlich gesagt?

segments.src: Anyone who needs this."
segments.tr: Jeder, der das braucht."

segments.src: That answer feels ambitious.
segments.tr: Diese Antwort klingt ehrgeizig.

segments.src: It's actually the most expensive sentence in business.
segments.tr: Es ist eigentlich der teuerste Satz im Geschäftsleben.

segments.src: If your customer is everyone, then your ad has to appeal to everyone, your price has to work for everyone, and your product has to be a little bit right for everyone — which usually means it's exactly right for no one.
segments.tr: Wenn Ihr Kunde jedermann ist, dann muss Ihre Werbung an alle appellieren, Ihr Preis muss für alle funktionieren, und Ihr Produkt muss ein wenig für alle recht sein — was normalerweise bedeutet, dass es für niemanden genau richtig ist.

segments.src: **Market segmentation** is the fix.
segments.tr: **Marktsegmentierung** ist die Lösung.

segments.src: It's the process of dividing a market into subgroups whose members are similar to each other and different from other groups in ways that *matter for buying behavior*.
segments.tr: Es ist der Prozess der Aufteilung eines Marktes in Untergruppen, deren Mitglieder sich ähneln und sich in Wegen unterscheiden, die *für das Kaufverhalten wichtig sind*.

segments.src: It's the "S" in the classic STP sequence: **Segmentation → Targeting → Positioning**.
segments.tr: Es ist das "S" in der klassischen STP-Sequenz: **Segmentierung → Targeting → Positionierung**.

segments.src: Segment first (how does this market naturally split?), then choose which slices to serve, then decide what you'll mean to them.
segments.tr: Segmentieren Sie zuerst (wie teilt sich dieser Markt natürlich auf?), dann wählen Sie, welche Scheiben bedient werden sollen, dann entscheiden Sie, was Sie ihnen bedeuten werden.

segments.src: One thing that trips people up: you don't *create* segments.
segments.tr: Eine Sache, die die Menschen verwirrt: Sie *erstellen* Segmente nicht.

segments.src: You *discover* them.
segments.tr: Sie *entdecken* sie.

segments.src: The differences are already out there in people's wallets and calendars.
segments.tr: Die Unterschiede sind bereits in den Geldbörsen und Kalendern der Menschen vorhanden.

segments.src: Your job is to find the cut lines that are real.
segments.tr: Ihre Aufgabe ist es, die Schnittlinien zu finden, die real sind.

segments.src: ### The four families of segmentation variables
segments.tr: ### Die vier Familien von Segmentierungsvariablen

segments.src: Marketers slice markets using four broad kinds of **bases** (the variables you cut on):
segments.tr: Vermarkter teilen Märkte mit vier breiten Arten von **Basen** (die Variablen, auf die Sie schneiden):

segments.src: - **Geographic** — region, climate, city vs. suburb, ZIP code. Snow blowers sell differently in Minneapolis than in Phoenix.
segments.tr: - **Geografisch** — Region, Klima, Stadt vs. Vorstadt, Postleitzahl. Schneefräsen werden in Minneapolis anders verkauft als in Phoenix.

segments.src: - **Demographic** — age, income, gender, household size, education, life stage. Easy to measure, easy to buy media against.
segments.tr: - **Demografisch** — Alter, Einkommen, Geschlecht, Haushaltsgröße, Bildung, Lebensphase. Leicht zu messen, leicht, Medien dagegen zu kaufen.

segments.src: - **Psychographic** — values, lifestyle, personality, self-image, identity. *Why* someone buys.
segments.tr: - **Psychografisch** — Werte, Lebensstil, Persönlichkeit, Selbstbild, Identität. *Warum* jemand kauft.

segments.src: - **Behavioral** — usage rate, purchase occasion, benefits sought, loyalty status, price sensitivity. *What they actually do.*
segments.tr: - **Verhaltensorientiert** — Nutzungsrate, Kaufgelegenheit, angestrebte Vorteile, Loyalitätsstatus, Preisempfindlichkeit. *Was sie tatsächlich tun.*

segments.src: Here's the practical hierarchy most experienced marketers land on.
segments.tr: Hier ist die praktische Hierarchie, auf die sich die meisten erfahrenen Vermarkter einigen.

segments.src: Demographics tell you **who**.
segments.tr: Die Demografie sagt dir, **wer**.

segments.src: Psychographics tell you **why**.
segments.tr: Psychografie sagt dir, **warum**.

segments.src: Behavior tells you **what they actually did with their money** — and behavior is usually the strongest predictor of what they'll do next.
segments.tr: Verhalten sagt dir, **was sie tatsächlich mit ihrem Geld getan haben** — und Verhalten ist normalerweise der stärkste Prädiktor dafür, was sie als nächstes tun werden.

segments.src: Two 34-year-olds in Austin with identical incomes can have nothing in common as customers; one buys the same brand for a decade, the other switches every time there's a coupon.
segments.tr: Zwei 34-Jährige in Austin mit identischen Einkommen können als Kunden nichts gemeinsam haben; einer kauft dieselbe Marke ein Jahrzehnt lang, der andere wechselt jedes Mal, wenn es einen Gutschein gibt.

segments.src: The catch: behavior is hard to observe *before* someone becomes a customer.
segments.tr: Der Haken: Verhalten ist schwer zu beobachten, *bevor* jemand Kunde wird.

segments.src: So the common workflow is to **segment on behavior and needs, then profile with demographics** — because demographics are what let you actually find these people in an ad platform, a mailing list, or a store location decision.
segments.tr: Der übliche Arbeitsablauf ist also, **nach Verhalten und Bedürfnissen zu segmentieren, dann mit Demografien zu profilieren** — weil die Demografie es Ihnen ermöglicht, diese Menschen in einer Anzeigenplattform, einer Mailingliste oder einer Geschäftslokationsentscheidung tatsächlich zu finden.

segments.src: ### When is a segment worth having?
segments.tr: ### Wann ist ein Segment wertvoll?

segments.src: Not every group you can name is a segment worth chasing.
segments.tr: Nicht jede Gruppe, die Sie benennen können, ist ein Segment, das es wert ist, verfolgt zu werden.

segments.src: The standard checklist:
segments.tr: Die standardmäßige Checkliste:

segments.src: - **Measurable** — you can size it and describe it.
segments.tr: - **Messbar** — Sie können seine Größe bestimmen und es beschreiben.

segments.src: - **Substantial** — big enough to be worth the effort.
segments.tr: - **Substanziell** — groß genug, um den Aufwand wert zu sein.

segments.src: - **Accessible** — you can actually reach it with media and distribution.
segments.tr: - **Zugänglich** — Sie können es tatsächlich mit Medien und Vertrieb erreichen.

segments.src: - **Differentiable** — it responds to your offer differently than other segments do. (This is the one people skip, and it's the one that makes segmentation *segmentation* rather than trivia.)
segments.tr: - **Unterscheidbar** — es reagiert auf Ihr Angebot anders als andere Segmente. (Dies ist derjenige, den Menschen überspringen, und es ist derjenige, der Segmentierung *Segmentierung* statt Trivialitäten macht.)

segments.src: - **Actionable** — you have the resources to serve it well.
segments.tr: - **Umsetzbar** — Sie haben die Ressourcen, um es gut zu bedienen.

segments.src: A rough way to size one, in plain arithmetic:
segments.tr: Eine grobe Möglichkeit, eine zu dimensionieren, in einfacher Arithmetik:

segments.src: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase
segments.tr: segment value = number of people × purchases per year × spend per purchase

segments.src: Then subtract what it costs to reach and serve them.
segments.tr: Dann subtrahieren Sie, was es kostet, sie zu erreichen und zu bedienen.

segments.src: A huge segment you can't reach cheaply is worth less than a small one that's easy to find.
segments.tr: Ein großes Segment, das Sie nicht billig erreichen können, ist weniger wert als ein kleines, das leicht zu finden ist.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life: The January Gym Rush
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag: Der Januar-Fitnessstudio-Ansturm

segments.src: Every January, roughly the same resolution — "get in shape" — sends millions of Americans looking for a gym.
segments.tr: Jeden Januar schickt ungefähr die gleiche Vorsatznahme — "in Form kommen" — Millionen von Amerikanern auf der Suche nach einem Fitnessstudio.

segments.src: From the outside it looks like one market.
segments.tr: Von außen sieht es wie ein Markt aus.

segments.src: It's at least four.
segments.tr: Es sind mindestens vier.

segments.src: **Planet Fitness** sells a Classic membership for around $15 a month, wraps the place in purple and yellow, and calls it a "Judgement Free Zone."
segments.tr: **Planet Fitness** verkauft eine Classic-Mitgliedschaft für etwa $15 pro Monat, hüllt den Ort in Lila und Gelb ein und nennt es eine "Urteilsfreie Zone".

segments.src: That tagline isn't decoration — it's a psychographic bullseye aimed at people who *want* to exercise but feel self-conscious walking past a row of grunting powerlifters.
segments.tr: Dieser Slogan ist keine Dekoration — es ist ein psychografisches Bullseye, das auf Menschen abzielt, die *möchten* trainieren, sich aber selbstbewusst fühlen, wenn sie an einer Reihe von grunzenden Gewichthebern vorbeigehen.

segments.src: Notice the behavioral angle too: a very low price across a very large member base works precisely because the average member doesn't show up all that often.
segments.tr: Beachten Sie auch die Verhaltensweise: Ein sehr niedriger Preis über eine sehr große Mitgliederbasis hinweg funktioniert genau deshalb, weil der Durchschnittsmitglied nicht so oft auftaucht.

segments.src: Light users are, unusually, the profitable ones.
segments.tr: Leichte Benutzer sind ungewöhnlich die rentablen.

segments.src: **Equinox** charges well north of $200 a month in major markets and, famously, once ran a campaign that said "We don't speak gym."
segments.tr: **Equinox** berechnet in den Hauptmärkten weit über 200 Dollar pro Monat und führte bekanntlich einmal eine Kampagne durch, die sagte "Wir sprechen kein Fitnessstudio".

segments.src: Same broad category, opposite segment: people for whom the club is a status good and a lifestyle signal, not a line item to minimize.
segments.tr: Gleiche breite Kategorie, entgegengesetztes Segment: Menschen, für die der Club ein Statusgut und ein Lebensstielsignal ist, nicht ein Posten zum Minimieren.

segments.src: **A CrossFit box** typically runs $150–$250 a month for something Planet Fitness deliberately doesn't sell — a coach who knows your name and a 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **Eine CrossFit-Box** läuft normalerweise $150–$250 pro Monat für etwas, das Planet Fitness absichtlich nicht verkauft — ein Trainer, der Ihren Namen kennt, und ein 6 Uhr morgens.

segments.src: class that notices when you're missing.
segments.tr: Klasse, die bemerkt, wenn Sie vermisst werden.

segments.src: The benefit sought is accountability and community.
segments.tr: Der angestrebte Vorteil ist Rechenschaftspflicht und Gemeinschaft.

segments.src: **The at-home buyer** — Peloton, a set of adjustable dumbbells, a YouTube subscription — is often segmented by life stage more than income: a parent with young kids who literally cannot leave the house at 6 a.m.
segments.tr: **Der At-Home-Käufer** — Peloton, ein Satz verstellbarer Hanteln, ein YouTube-Abonnement — wird oft mehr nach Lebensphase als nach Einkommen segmentiert: ein Elternteil mit kleinen Kindern, das buchstäblich nicht um 6 Uhr morgens aus dem Haus gehen kann.

segments.src: Now the important part.
segments.tr: Jetzt der wichtige Teil.

segments.src: Equinox is not losing to Planet Fitness.
segments.tr: Equinox verliert nicht gegen Planet Fitness.

segments.src: They are barely in the same fight.
segments.tr: Sie sind kaum im gleichen Kampf.

segments.src: Each one built a product, a price, a location strategy, and a tone of voice around a group that behaves differently — and each would damage itself trying to win the others.
segments.tr: Jeder baute ein Produkt, einen Preis, eine Standortstrategie und einen Tonfall um eine Gruppe, die sich anders verhält — und jeder würde sich selbst beschädigen, wenn er versuchte, die anderen zu gewinnen.

segments.src: A $15 Equinox would destroy its own signal.
segments.tr: Ein $15 Equinox würde sein eigenes Signal zerstören.

segments.src: A Planet Fitness with personal coaches in every corner would blow up its cost structure and scare off the exact people it was built for.
segments.tr: Ein Planet Fitness mit persönlichen Trainern in jeder Ecke würde seine Kostenstruktur aufblasen und die genauen Menschen abschrecken, für die es gebaut wurde.

segments.src: That's segmentation doing its job: not describing customers, but *deciding what you're willing to be bad at*.
segments.tr: Das ist Segmentierung bei der Arbeit: nicht Kunden beschreiben, sondern *entscheiden, wofür Sie bereit sind, schlecht zu sein*.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. Segmentation splits a broad market into groups that respond differently — it's the first step of STP, and "everyone" is not a segment.
segments.tr: 1. Segmentierung teilt einen breiten Markt in Gruppen auf, die unterschiedlich reagieren — es ist der erste Schritt von STP, und "jeder" ist kein Segment.

segments.src: 2. The four bases are geographic, demographic, psychographic, and behavioral; behavior predicts best, demographics reach best, so most marketers segment on behavior and profile with demographics.
segments.tr: 2. Die vier Basen sind geografisch, demografisch, psychografisch und verhaltensorientiert; Verhalten prognostiziert am besten, Demografie erreicht am besten, daher segmentieren die meisten Vermarkter nach Verhalten und profilieren mit Demografien.

segments.src: 3. A segment is only worth serving if it's measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable, and actionable — the differentiable test is the one that separates real segments from trivia.
segments.tr: 3. Ein Segment ist nur dann wert bedient zu werden, wenn es messbar, substanziell, zugänglich, unterscheidbar und umsetzbar ist — der unterscheidbare Test ist derjenige, der echte Segmente von Trivialitäten trennt.
